bet.text: CRESCENDO is a passing game, not a cycling game: pass notes to your own side fast, then shoot them all at once.

demand.text: Speaker scoring with the amplification bonus. The team believed notes already waiting on its side make the maximum bonus much easier to get. A small, very fast robot would move them there.

auto.text: The auto path ended behind the truss in a few championship matches and the shots still went in.

cycle.text: At Kettering the under-bumper intake either passed across the field through its own rollers or sent the note to the main shooter, which Limelights aimed, setting speed by distance to about 12 ft.
From Livonia on, the new shooter was more consistent back to the wing line.

endgame.text: From Livonia on, a fast last-second side climb: a mast whose spring-loaded hook pops out and grabs one chain link.

gave_up.text: The trap mechanism had to go, so the robot did not score in the trap at Kettering.
Small size meant tight packaging: the intake looks chaotic so the note can get through every bend ready to shoot.

changed.text: By Kettering a flip-up hood had replaced an amp diverter that did not work well.
Livonia brought a new shooter and the climb, the state championship a fourth Limelight, and a full-width compliant roller replaced intake flappers that let notes fly off on new carpet.

outcome.text: 49-17-2 in official play; ranked 9 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 56.14, Hopper).

solves.text: Win contested notes against other teams

facts.text: Three Krakens, because the intake also works as a shooter
A full-width compliant front roller replaced the vertical flappers after week 1 and worked for the rest of the season
Notes go through tight bends and reach the shooter ready to shoot

cost.text: The first version's flappers worked in the shop, but with new notes on new carpet the notes flew away
